correctness.rationale: Every crossed pair has exactly one transverse intersection almost surely: an overlap of vertical intervals has horizontal relative excursion at most one circumference. The conditional crossing probability is therefore interval length divided by circumference. Uniform-slope averaging, the exact overlap kernel and a four-region symbolic integration reproduce the exact number. Both direct intersection sampling and symbolic verification were executed; no numerical estimate substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The natural geodesic-crossing statistic of a standard finite flat cylinder is a global random-geometry observable. Its exact dimensionless value is independent of all aspect ratios even though the vertical and horizontal displacement laws are geometrically different, contrasting sharply with the closed two-periodic torus. This is a complete natural classification across the two-parameter geometric family, not a routine arbitrary numerical case.
